title: A raíz de que: como consecuencia directa de que (algo ocurriera)

sections.content: A raíz de que (as a direct result of, in the wake of) introduces a clause naming the specific event that triggered what follows. Unlike a raíz de + noun, a raíz de que is followed by a full clause, usually in the subjunctive, since it frames the triggering event as the cause rather than asserting it independently. These sentences are taken directly from the previous reading.

items.spanish: El asesinato de Colosio conmocionó al país entero y, a raíz de que ocurriera en plena carrera electoral, sembró una enorme incertidumbre política.
items.english: Colosio's assassination shocked the entire country and, as a direct result of its happening in the middle of the campaign, sowed enormous political uncertainty.

items.spanish: A raíz de que se agotaran las reservas internacionales del Banco de México, su gobierno se vio obligado a devaluar el peso mexicano de forma abrupta.
items.english: As a direct result of the Bank of Mexico's international reserves running out, his government was forced to abruptly devalue the Mexican peso.

items.spanish: Esta devaluación, a raíz de que amenazara con extenderse a otras economías emergentes de la región, llevó a Estados Unidos a organizar un rescate financiero de emergencia.
items.english: This devaluation, as a direct result of its threatening to spread to other emerging economies in the region, led the United States to organize an emergency financial bailout.

items.spanish: A raíz de que la apertura comercial coincidiera con una fragilidad institucional y financiera tan marcada, la modernización mexicana de los noventa avanzó siempre bajo la sombra de esa doble crisis.
items.english: As a direct result of trade opening coinciding with such marked institutional and financial fragility, Mexico's modernization in the nineties always advanced under the shadow of that double crisis.

sections.content: Compare a raíz de (+ noun, no subjunctive needed: a raíz de la crisis) with a raíz de que (+ clause, usually subjunctive: a raíz de que se agotaran las reservas). Both point to a direct trigger, but only the second names a full event with its own subject and verb.
